events.title: MTN MoMo interoperability with banks

events.title: Bank of Ghana e-cedi pilot

events.description: Telecel Group completed acquisition of Vodafone Ghana's operations, rebranding the operator.

events.title: mPharma expands pharmacy retail network
events.description: mPharma scaled its drug-store retail network across Ghana and other African markets.

events.title: GhanaWeb remains leading Ghanaian digital media property

signals.title: MTN Ghana deepens AI and fintech investment
signals.description: MTN Group-wide fintech and AI strategy is reflected in MoMo product expansion in Ghana.
signals.strategic_interpretation: The largest distribution network in Ghana's digital economy continues to compound fintech advantage; competitors must differentiate on service, not reach.

signals.title: Central bank digital currency pilot progresses
signals.description: e-cedi pilot continues, signalling direction of travel for digital payments regulation.
signals.strategic_interpretation: A state-backed digital currency would reshape the payments layer every Ghanaian fintech builds on.

signals.title: Hubtel maintains entrenched merchant distribution
signals.description: Hubtel remains the incumbent merchant payments and messaging platform in Ghana.
signals.strategic_interpretation: Incumbent distribution is Hubtel's core moat; new entrants must attack underserved segments rather than head-on.

signals.title: Zeepay strengthens cross-border remittance rails
signals.description: Continued international remittance partnerships expand Zeepay's footprint beyond Ghana.
signals.strategic_interpretation: Cross-border rails are a defensible niche where Ghanaian fintechs can own corridors.

signals.title: mPharma among Africa's most funded healthtechs
signals.description: mPharma's cumulative venture funding makes it a leading African healthtech with Accra roots.
signals.strategic_interpretation: Pharmaceutical supply-chain data is a strategic asset; healthtech consolidation will centre on distribution data.

signals.title: Farmerline scales Mergdata across agribusinesses
signals.description: Farmerline's farm-data platform continues to onboard agribusiness clients across Africa.
signals.strategic_interpretation: Farm-level data captured by Mergdata is foundational for agri-finance and insurance products.

opportunities.title: AI-native construction cost database for Ghana
opportunities.problem: No transparent, continuously updated source of construction costs for Ghana exists; estimators rely on manual rate books and anecdote.
opportunities.market: Construction cost intelligence for Ghana's AEC industry: contractors, quantity surveyors, developers, banks and government.
existing_alternatives: International cost databases with weak Ghana coverage
opportunities.why_now: Falling AI costs make dynamic cost estimation feasible; Ghana's construction sector lacks data infrastructure.
opportunities.potential_customers: Quantity surveying firms, contractors, developers, project financiers

opportunities.title: API aggregation layer for Ghanaian financial services
opportunities.problem: Fintechs must integrate bank, mobile-money and payments APIs individually; a unified abstraction layer is missing.
opportunities.market: Ghana fintechs, banks, and international companies expanding into Ghana.
existing_alternatives: Pan-African aggregators with thin Ghana coverage
opportunities.why_now: Open-banking direction from the regulator and rising fintech density create demand.

opportunities.title: Farm-level data layer for agri-finance
opportunities.problem: Banks and insurers cannot underwrite smallholder agriculture because farm-level data is fragmented.
opportunities.market: Agricultural lending, crop insurance and input credit in Ghana.
opportunities.why_now: Mobile money distribution + satellite data make farm-level scoring newly viable.

opportunities.title: AI workflows for Ghanaian AEC firms (BIM-to-cost)
opportunities.problem: Ghanaian AEC firms underuse BIM and have no automated path from design models to cost intelligence.
opportunities.market: Architects, engineers, quantity surveyors and contractors in Ghana.
existing_alternatives: International BIM tools with local cost data gaps
opportunities.why_now: AI can bridge design-to-estimate; local cost data is the differentiator.

opportunities.title: African-language voice interfaces for rural services
opportunities.problem: Digital services exclude users who are not literate in English; Twi and other Ghanaian languages lack production voice AI.
opportunities.market: Rural financial services, agriculture advisory, health information.
opportunities.why_now: Foundation-model speech technology is improving for low-resource languages; Ghana's languages are under-served.

opportunities.title: Cybersecurity services for Ghanaian SMEs and fintechs
opportunities.problem: Digitalisation is outpacing security capacity; SMEs and fintechs lack affordable security operations.
opportunities.market: Ghanaian SMEs, fintechs, banks and public institutions.
opportunities.why_now: Cyber Security Act 2020 mandates protections; incident volume is rising with digitalisation.

regulations.body: Establishes the Cyber Security Authority and obligations for critical information infrastructure and service providers.

regulations.title: Electronic Transactions Act 2008 (Act 772)
regulations.body: Legal framework for electronic transactions, e-commerce and electronic communications.

regulations.title: National Digital Economy Policy
regulations.body: Policy framework for Ghana's digital transformation, digital identity, payments and digital skills.

reports.title: Ghana Technology Power Map — Market Overview

content.executive_summary: Ghana's technology economy is anchored by mobile money, fintech and telecom infrastructure, with emerging strength in agritech, healthtech and AI services. Accra concentrates most venture activity; Kumasi anchors agritech and engineering talent.

Ghana's fintech market is mature by African standards, driven by mobile money ubiquity and a pragmatic regulator. Incumbents hold distribution; new value is being created in SME financial operations, cross-border rails and infrastructure layers.

Construction technology in Ghana is early: BIM adoption is limited, cost data is fragmented, and few dedicated local players exist. This represents a genuine white space for cost intelligence and AI-enabled AEC workflows.

AI activity in Ghana is accelerating: data-services firms, university research and adoption inside large corporates. African-language AI and AI-for-agriculture are emerging niches with global relevance.
